Throughput checkpoint: n/a, read-only investigation.### Overview

`add` in `calc.js` concatenates two numeric strings. It does not add them as numbers. `add("2", "3")` returns `"23"`, not `5`. The function is a bare wrapper around JavaScript's `+` operator. It does not validate, coerce, or check argument types.

The workspace has no callers, tests, or docs that define intended string behavior. Measured from the source and a Node check by [Explain add numeric strings](12b18e71-1170-4f2c-9d1f-043d7283a702).

### How it works

```1:3:/private/tmp/cursor-live/calc.js
export function add(a, b) {
  return a + b;
}
```

When `add("2", "3")` runs, both arguments stay strings and go into `a + b`. If either operand is a string, JavaScript converts the other to a string and joins them. Numeric addition happens only when neither operand is a string. So the result is `"23"`.

|---|---|---|
| `add("2", "3")` | `"23"` | `string` |
| `add(2, "3")` | `"23"` | `string` |
